chapter_title: [C]oncerning the Father of Gr[eat]ness: [ho]w he i
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶2:**
Immeasurably great is [GAP-1: the infinite domain of] divine wisdom [GAP-2: that exists] by virtue of the Divine Itself, the first origin of all being. How the Divine is and subsists in His five essential faculties of wisdom — which are [GAP-3: the boundless interior capacities,] having neither limit nor measure to [GAP-4: their fullness —] divine intelligence, divine thought, divine perception, divine providence, and [GAP-5: divine reflection;] and His twelve faculties of wisdom, which are His twelve modes of omniscience in their completeness.

---

**¶3:**
Now, five essential faculties of wisdom dwell within each heavenly sphere, [GAP-6: and from each] five great influxes of celestial acknowledgment flow [GAP-7: forth, and] five great [GAP-8: emanations of] wis[GAP-9: dom proceed from them.]

---

**¶4:**
The first is His wisdom that illumi[GAP-10: nates all things;] it flowed forth from Him and pour[GAP-11: ed into] all heavenly spheres.

---

**¶5:**
The second is the sphere of perception of [GAP-12: divine good, which issues from Him] and pervades all the heavenly spheres of the Divine.

---

**¶6:**
The third is His living divine truth — the proceeding Word — of [GAP-13: power, which resounds throughout] all His heavenly spheres [GAP-14: and gives them form.]

---

**¶7:**
The fourth is His [GAP-15: blessed]-ness, [GAP-16: which] flows forth from Him [GAP-17: through]out [GAP-18: all spheres.]

---

**¶8:**
The fif[th] is His great glori[GAP-19: ous presence,] that [GAP-20: divine delight] which [has been manifest] through all states, whi[ch contin]ues [GAP-21: to pervade] all of them. It was inscribed into them — [GAP-22: an interior form] sealed in [GAP-23: their inmost being,] sealed [GAP-24: as a living imprint.] As they send forth [GAP-25: their worship] in [GAP-26: reciprocal communion,] they too receive spiritual sustenance [GAP-27: from the Divine,] and immediately [GAP-28: through His] living divine tru[GAP-29: th they are filled with] celestial joy, [GAP-30: and their interior life is] established anew. It shall flow forth from it [GAP-31: unceasingly, and] they shall [GAP-32: receive abundantly] and become rich in the [GAP-33: fullness of wisdom. This] too is beautiful — [GAP-34: the living] image [GAP-35: of the Divine,] the interior formation [GAP-36: of heavenly order —] and they live [GAP-37: in this state of celestial blessedness] forever.

---

### Summary Note

This passage describes the Divine Itself not as a cosmic geography but as the infinite interior reality of Divine Love and Wisdom — how the Lord's essential being subsists in five faculties (intelligence, thought, perception, providence, reflection), and how these unfold into twelve complete modes of omniscience. The five "gushings" correspond to the fivefold influx from the Divine into all heavenly spheres: illuminating wisdom, the sphere of celestial good perceived as fragrance, proceeding truth as the living Word, the state of blessedness, and the manifest presence of divine delight. The "sealing" and "sculpting" describe how divine order is not imposed externally but inscribed as a living form within each receiving vessel, which then reciprocates through worship and receives sustenance — the eternal circuit of influx and return that constitutes heavenly life.

fills.explanation: Confirming editor's choice: "the land of light" is the standard Kephalaia designation for the Father's infinite domain, and the spiritual reading's "infinite domain of" maps directly to "land of" in Manichaean natural-register vocabulary.
The spiritual reading confirms "that exists" — the clause introduces the Father of Greatness as the cause of the land of light's existence, requiring a relative clause linking the two.
The five light limbs are being identified as the storehouses; "called" naturally introduces this identification in Kephalaia register ("which are called the storehouses").
Completing "them" and bridging to the enumeration of the five faculties; the spiritual reading confirms a transition from the limitless storehouses to naming the five attributes.
Completing the fifth faculty "consideration" and connecting to the twelve wisdoms with a simple conjunction, as the spiritual reading indicates a transition from the five to the twelve.
The spiritual reading confirms "and from each" — the five faculties in each sphere produce five corresponding emanations, requiring a distributive connector.
Completing "forth" and connecting to the parallel second set of five with a conjunction, as confirmed by the spiritual reading's "forth, and."
The spiritual reading specifies "emanations of" — the second set of five are emanations of light, parallel to the "springs of praise" in the first set.
Completing "light" and adding the emanation formula; "shine forth" is fitting for light specifically, and the spiritual reading confirms these emanations proceed outward from the spheres.
Completing "enlightens" and adding the universal object; the spiritual reading confirms "nates all things" (illuminates all things), and the first emanation is light that enlightens universally.
Completing "poured" and connecting to "all aeons" with the directional preposition; the spiritual reading confirms "ed into" as the light flows into all heavenly spheres.
The second emanation is the Father's perfume; the spiritual reading confirms it "issues from Him," and "gushes" maintains the passage's consistent spring/gushing vocabulary.

The living voice (proceeding divine truth) is characterized by power and fills all aeons; the spiritual reading confirms "power, which resounds throughout" and the medium gap is strongly constrained by the voice-aeon structure.
The spiritual reading says the voice "gives them form"; in Kephalaia register, the voice's pervading activity is expressed as filling the aeons, completing the sentence about the third emanation.

The fourth emanation corresponds to the sense of taste in the five-senses framework; "sweetness" is the natural-register term for what Swedenborg calls "blessedness" — the perception of divine good experienced as spiritual sweetness.
A relative pronoun connecting "sweetness" to the verb "gushes forth," paralleling the relative clauses used for the other emanations in the passage.
Combining with the adjacent "ut" to form "throughout"; the spiritual reading confirms the sweetness extends "throughout" all spheres, and this matches the passage's pervading-emanation pattern.
The spiritual reading confirms "all spheres" which in Kephalaia natural register is "all the aeons" — the standard term for heavenly spheres throughout this passage.

Completing "glorious" and adding "image" — the fifth emanation is the divine form/image, confirmed by the subsequent sculpting and sealing language; "image" corresponds to the spiritual reading's "presence" as visible divine manifestation.
The spiritual reading says "divine delight" — in Kephalaia natural register this is "joy," serving as an appositive that identifies the glorious image with the experiential quality of divine joy.
The spiritual reading says "to pervade" — in the natural register "continues in all of them" expresses the ongoing pervasive presence of the divine image within each aeon.
The spiritual reading says "an interior form" — the divine image is sculpted in the aeons as a form, establishing the interior pattern that is then sealed; this bridges the sculpting to the sealing.
Completing "them" and connecting to the second instance of "sealed" with a conjunction; the spiritual reading indicates sequential sealing actions.
The spiritual reading says "as a living imprint" — in Kephalaia register "living image" expresses the seal as a dynamic, vital inscription of the divine form rather than a static impression.
The spiritual reading says "their worship" — in Kephalaia register "praise" is the standard term for reciprocal acknowledgment sent from the aeons back to the divine source.
The spiritual reading confirms "from the Divine" — in natural register "from him" identifies the Father as the source of nourishment received in return for the praise sent forth.
The spiritual reading confirms "through His" — the living voice is the medium through which nourishment and renewal are conveyed, expressing the instrumentality of divine truth.
Completing "voice" and introducing the result of the living voice's action; the spiritual reading confirms the aeons are "filled with" celestial joy through the divine truth.
The spiritual reading says "and their interior life is" — in simpler Kephalaia register "and they are set up anew" expresses the renewal of the aeons' life through divine influx.
The spiritual reading says "unceasingly, and" — the gushing forth is perpetual, expressing the unbroken character of divine influx that Swedenborg describes as continuous creation.
The spiritual reading says "receive abundantly" — "receive" is the Kephalaia's natural term for the vessels' acceptance of divine influx, with the subsequent "become rich" conveying the abundance.

The spiritual reading says "fullness of wisdom. This" — in the Kephalaia's natural register, "light" is the term for what Swedenborg calls wisdom; "This" begins a new sentence about the beauty of the divine image.

The spiritual reading says "the living" modifies the portrayal/image — "beautiful in the living portrayal" expresses that the beauty resides in the vital, dynamic quality of the divine image inscribed within.

Completing "portrayal" and specifying it as the Father's portrayal; the spiritual reading says "of the Divine, the interior formation" — "of the Father" is the Kephalaia's natural-register term for the divine source.
The spiritual reading says "of heavenly order" — in Kephalaia register "of the aeons" specifies that the adornment belongs to and structures the heavenly spheres.
